info.title: API.SH: GitLab
info.description: The GitLab API from API.SH: public GitLab data as clean JSON. Every endpoint is a GET with query parameters and your key in the x-api-key header. Calls that run cost the credits shown (x-credits): successes, and lookups that found nothing (404). Refused calls and errors on our side are free. Docs: https://api.sh/docs · Every platform: https://api.sh/openapi.json

get.description:
Merge requests of a public gitlab.com project: id, number, title, link, state, author, assignees and reviewers, labels, milestone, source and target branches, dates (created, updated, merged, closed), merged by, merge status, draft flag, votes, comment count and the description (first 4,000 characters). Pass `next_page` back as `page`; null on the last page. Pass `iid` for one merge request with more detail, and `include=changes,approvals` for its file changes and approvals.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/gitlab-project-merge-requests

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Project path (namespace/project), its gitlab.com link, or the numeric project id.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search words in title and description.

parameters.name: iid
parameters.description: One merge request by its number (the number in its URL). The answer then holds it in `items` and `item`, with its full reference, number of changed files, conflicts flag, merge and squash commits, diff refs, latest pipeline (status, ref, duration), time tracking and closed by.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: With `iid`, comma separated: `changes` (each changed file: old and new path, new, renamed, deleted or generated flags and the diff, first 20,000 characters per file; up to 100 files) and `approvals` (approved, approvals required and left, who approved). Each costs one more upstream request.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Create keys at https://app.api.sh/keys. Authorization: Bearer <key> also works.

raw.name: raw
raw.description: 0 leaves out the bulky `raw` source blocks (often 10-30x smaller).

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. `posts.id,posts.title`. Call metadata is always included.

fresh.name: fresh
fresh.description: 1 skips the 24-hour cache and fetches live.

output.name: output
output.description: csv or ndjson returns the response's records (its main list, or the object as one row) as CSV or NDJSON instead of JSON.

records.name: records
records.description: With output=csv|ndjson: the top-level list to turn into rows (e.g. `reviews`), or `.` for the whole object as one row.

status_url.description: On a 503 for a paused endpoint: the status page, which lists open incidents.

E400.description: A parameter is missing or invalid. Not charged (unless the call ran and the source rejected the value; credits_used says).

E401.description: Missing, invalid, revoked or expired API key. Not charged. See https://api.sh/docs/errors#401

E402.description: Not enough credits, a spend limit you set was reached (`spend_limit`), or the key's monthly credit cap was reached (`key_cap`). Not charged.

E404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

E502.description: The source site failed this time; retry. Not charged.

E503.description: Endpoint paused or temporarily unavailable; may include retry-after, and status_url (https://api.sh/status) for a paused endpoint. Not charged.
